title: Worship God Not Angels
definition: The doctrine of Worship God Not Angels teaches that scripture forbids the worship of angels because worship belongs to God alone.
summary: Worship God Not Angels names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. Scripture forbids the worship of angels because worship belongs to God alone. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to Worship God Not Angels because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: Scripture forbids the worship of angels because worship belongs to God alone. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because spiritual fascination can become idolatry when created servants receive the attention due to the Creator. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Refuse every form of angel-centered devotion. Thank God for His servants, but bow only before the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
